page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a general-purpose cloud instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. Powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor family running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) alongside hardware encryption acceleration through AES and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Memory subsystem benchmarks demonstrate high throughput, registering 530.35 GB/sec on uncached read operations and 259.87 GB/sec on large block write operations. Bundled local storage is limited to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without integrated hardware GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks place the instance in high tiers for general computing, compilation, and data processing. It achieved 2,775.0 on single-core and 25,521.0 on multi-core Geekbench testing, with software compilation scores reaching 63,309.0. PassMark evaluation demonstrated a CPU score of 98,888.12 and 41,716.12 in database operations, while Redis SET throughput reached 111.5 million operations per second. CPU-based small language model execution demonstrated 5,731.94 prompt tokens per second and 391.46 generation tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

Given the minimal local storage capacity of 1 GB NVMe, operational deployments require network storage volumes for stateful data retention. The configuration is well suited for memory-intensive backend applications, continuous integration build clusters, batch compilation pipelines, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, and microservice orchestration.
description: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g is a general-purpose virtual machine in the VX1 Cloud Compute family, featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 256.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes advanced vector extensions like AVX-512 alongside hardware AES encryption. There are no GPU accelerators, and local storage is constrained to 1 GB of NVMe SSD space, making external network storage necessary for data-heavy workloads. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded processing, scoring 25,521.0 in multi-core Geekbench and achieving 111.5 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. With its balanced compute-to-memory profile and high memory bandwidth, the server is suitable for CPU-bound compilation pipelines, in-memory caching nodes, microservice application backends, and container orchestration clusters.
